conceptZh: 矮胖的戰鬥機器人用積木蓋山：左右兩根疊得剛剛好，他站上中間那根想再加一塊，結果中間柱子一直往上長，把他舉得超高，他在頂端手忙腳亂地揮手，最後滑桿溜下來；一條長積木從底下滑進來把三根接起來，變成「山」。
object: a stubby armored toy battle robot and stacks of chunky interlocking plastic bricks
morph: three brick columns rise with the middle one tallest and a long flat brick slides in beneath them, joining their feet into the base stroke of 山
creativeAngle: 第一次為「山」補上 prompt。用孩子喜歡的戰鬥機器人加樂高積木，笑點是「柱子自己一直長高，把蓋房子的人舉到天上」的尺寸落差，而這個動作本身就是中間那一豎變長的筆劃邏輯。語音詞選「火山」，火ㄏㄨㄛˇ、山ㄕㄢ都是單一讀音，且火是他已經學過的字。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second 3D stylized toy animation as one continuous locked-off shot on a clean solid light-cream background. A stubby, friendly toy battle robot with rounded armored shoulders and stompy feet is busy building with chunky interlocking plastic bricks, centered in frame. From 0.3 to 1.6 seconds he snaps together a short column of deep teal bricks on the left and a matching short column on the right, dusts off his hands, and nods with satisfaction. At 1.8 seconds he climbs onto the low middle stack to add one more brick on top, but the middle column keeps growing under his feet, brick after brick, lifting him far too high above his own building; he wobbles at the top, pedals his little arms in comic surprise, and freezes wide-eyed for a beat. At 3.2 seconds he gives up, hugs the column and slides all the way down it like a fire pole, landing with a soft thump and a puff of pride. At 3.8 seconds one long flat brick glides in from below and clicks across the feet of all three columns, joining them into a single base. The robot stomps out of frame to the left by 4.7 seconds. By 5.0 seconds the build has resolved into one correctly formed Traditional Chinese character 山 in saturated deep teal, perfectly centered and uncropped, filling about 70% of the frame height with generous margins on all sides: one tall centre stroke, a shorter stroke on each side, and one clean horizontal base, all crisp and clearly separated. From 5.0 to 8.0 seconds the frame holds completely still on 山 with nothing else moving in the shot. Style: Pixar-like glossy chunky toy materials, soft studio lighting, bright high-contrast but not neon colors, no dark or moody grading. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin and says exactly 「山、山、火山」, using the reading ㄕㄢ for 山 both times and in the word. Speak the first 山 around 0.5 seconds, the second around 2.0 seconds, and 火山 around 5.6 seconds during the still hold, with natural pauses, then stop; do not keep chanting the character or repeat the line. Keep the brick clicks and the thump soft and clear of the voice, and use no music louder than the voice. The spoken word is audio only: add no volcano, lava, smoke or fire imagery of any kind. The only writing anywhere in the frame is the single character 山: no subtitles, no vocabulary text, no other letters, numbers, watermarks, scenery, extra props, particles, lens flare, motion blur on the glyph, or flashing effects.

conceptZh: 積木小隊排成中高兩低的山形，得意敬禮卻一起向前仆倒；大家重新站穩，連著底座變成清楚的「山」。
object: An original squad of expressive deep-teal interlocking building bricks
morph: Three brick columns recover from a synchronized forward topple and stand on a continuous brick base, forming the tall central vertical, shorter outer uprights, and connected bottom of 山.
creativeAngle: 讓積木自己當主角：小隊太認真敬禮，整排山峰竟一起仆倒，眼睛還偷偷往上看。笑點來自整齊隊伍的同步失誤，再用重新站穩的動作呈現「山」的中高兩低結構。
promptEn:
Create an exactly 8-second stylized 3D toy animation featuring an original squad of interlocking building bricks: eager, overly disciplined little performers with tiny expressive eyes and retractable toy feet. Use saturated deep-teal plastic, a pale warm-peach studio background, soft lighting, and a clean centered composition. One continuous shot, with enough margin to contain every movement.

At the opening, the squad is already marching its last few steps into position. By 1.2 seconds, the bricks have climbed onto one another to make three square-ended columns on a continuous horizontal brick base: the middle column noticeably tallest, the outer two equally shorter, suggesting three mountain peaks. Their eyes glance proudly along the formation. After a brief self-satisfied pause, all three columns attempt an excessively formal forward bow. They lean too far! Between 1.8 and 2.8 seconds, the entire columns pivot forward at their feet and flop flat toward the camera in one synchronized plastic patter; the extra-long middle column lands with one additional soft tap. Hold the flattened formation for a small comic beat as their eyes look upward together, pretending everything went according to plan. Keep the base fixed and every brick attached to its column, making the mishap immediately understandable.

From 3.2 to 4.6 seconds, their tiny feet push against the floor and lever the three columns upright again. The outer columns check the middle column, then all three settle firmly into their correct positions. Eyes and feet retract flush into the plastic. As they recover, the camera eases into a perfectly straight-on view, eliminating visible depth overlaps. By 4.6 seconds, the bricks form one correctly proportioned Traditional Chinese glyph 山, centered and uncropped at about 70% of frame height. Its central vertical rises highest; the shorter left upright turns into the continuous bottom horizontal, and the shorter right upright meets that horizontal at its right endpoint. The central vertical joins the same base. Preserve two spacious open areas between the uprights, square corners, consistent stroke thickness, and an uninterrupted solid-color silhouette; brick seams are subtle and never split a stroke. Hold this finished glyph completely still from 4.6 through 8.0 seconds.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks clear Taiwanese Mandarin, saying exactly 「山、山、山頂」. Say the first 山 around 0.4 seconds, the second around 3.5 seconds, and 山頂 around 5.5 seconds while the finished glyph is clearly held. Use the reading ㄕㄢ throughout, with relaxed natural pauses, and stop after 山頂. Keep the marching clicks and comic landing soft beneath the voice; use no music. The single target glyph 山 is the only on-screen writing. Keep the vocabulary audio-only, with no subtitles, logos, watermarks, extra props, scenery, clutter, or flashing effects.
